status_summary: CMS announced on 2025-06-03 that HHS and CMS were rescinding the July 2022 EMTALA guidance (QSO-22-22-Hospitals) and the former Secretary's accompanying letter, saying they do not reflect current administration policy, while stating that CMS will keep enforcing EMTALA and will address legal confusion it attributes to the prior administration. A Congressional Research Service report updated 2026-07-20 confirms the June 2025 rescission, identifies no replacement guidance, and says the parties agreed in March 2025 to dismiss the federal suit against Idaho; St. Luke's Health System's own suit led to an injunction limiting enforcement of the state ban against that provider. The CRS report describes Texas v. Becerra as ending in an injunction against the 2022 guidance in Texas and as to the plaintiffs, affirmed by the Fifth Circuit, while CMS's EMTALA web page (last modified 2026-03-10) still links the 2022 guidance and notes that injunction without mentioning the rescission. A July 2026 CMS proposed rule on accreditation organization checks of some EMTALA administrative requirements was finalized in the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC final rule (FR Doc. 2026-22739, published 2026-11-06, effective 2027-01-01); it concerns administrative requirements and does not restore or replace the rescinded guidance. Whether CMS and state agency investigations of alleged refusals to perform abortions ended was not verified.

timeline.event: The Justice Department drops the Biden-era suit against Idaho over whether EMTALA requires emergency abortions (early March 2025; exact day not given, first of month used); St. Luke's Health System's own suit continues and a federal judge in that case issues an injunction protecting its doctors from prosecution under the state ban.

HHS and CMS rescind the July 2022 EMTALA guidance and the former Secretary's accompanying letter, saying the guidance does not reflect administration policy; CMS says it will continue to enforce EMTALA and address legal confusion from the prior administration.

CMS's EMTALA page, last modified on this date, still links the July 2022 guidance (QSO-22-22) with a note on the preliminary injunction in Texas v. Becerra (N.D. Tex., No. 5:22-CV-185-H, limited to Texas and to members of two named medical associations) and does not mention a rescission.

A Congressional Research Service report (updated this date) states that CMS rescinded the 2022 EMTALA guidance in June 2025, identifies no replacement, records the March 2025 agreed dismissal of the Idaho case, and describes a July 2026 CMS proposed rule on accreditation-organization checks of some EMTALA administrative requirements.

CMS publishes the CY 2027 OPPS/ASC final rule with comment period (CMS-1850-FC, FR Doc. 2026-22739, effective 2027-01-01), finalizing that hospital accrediting organizations with deeming authority may assess certain EMTALA administrative requirements under 42 CFR 489.20 during surveys; the portion read does not mention abortion or the rescinded 2022 guidance, so it is context for this objective.

title: Rescind the 2022 EMTALA abortion guidance and end related enforcement and suits
uncertainties: The rescission is documented by a CMS statement, a States Newsroom report and a CRS report (which gives June 2025 without a day); the CMS memo itself was not reached, and CMS's EMTALA page last modified 2026-03-10 does not mention it, which may mean the page was not updated rather than that the rescission did not occur. The CRS and law-firm accounts do not date the Texas v. Becerra and St. Luke's rulings, and the CRS description of Texas v. Becerra (permanent injunction affirmed by the Fifth Circuit) differs from the 'preliminary injunction' wording on CMS's page. The CRS dates the July 2026 proposed rule's Federal Register publication 2026-07-07 while the Goodwin alert says 2026-07-02. Not checked: CMS or state agency investigation practice and DOJ positions in other states. The Mandate's separate p. 474 recommendations (investigating born-alive infants under EMTALA and Section 504, reviving a 2020 proposed regulation, and the Born-Alive Abortion Survivors Protection Act) are not covered by this record. The final rule text was read only in part (the portion listing the specific 42 CFR 489.20 requirements assessed by accrediting organizations was not reached), so the statement that it does not address the 2022 abortion guidance rests on the summary and fact sheet and the visible text; an independent review on 2026-11-06 found no mention of abortion or of the 2022 guidance in about the first 100,000 of 117,271 characters of the public inspection copy. The rule is treated as context, not as an action on this objective. Whether CMS and state agency investigations of alleged refusals to perform abortions ended was still not verified.
